A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same W2SD research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-mixture and CIFAR-10 experiments, image-generation evaluations, personalization studies, and video-generation results, including Tables 1–14.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds trajectory-alignment analyses and an evaluated Auto-guidance comparison in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains strong-model denoising followed by weak-model inversion, with the same weight, condition, and pipeline pairings. The supplementary Re-Sampling algorithms are also retained. Corrections to the mathematical characterization do not establish a changed sampling procedure.

E1.justification: The documented coverage remains Gaussian mixtures, CIFAR-10, ImageNet, Pick-a-Pic, DrawBench, GenEval, personalized generation, and VBench video generation. The added appendix analyses reuse existing domains and generation tasks; no distinct new dataset or task coverage is established.

E2.justification: v3 newly evaluates Auto-guidance against W2SD using the human-preference model and SDXL pairing, reporting Table 15 and Figure 23. Earlier comparator memberships, including the selected-noise Re-Sampling comparisons, remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New Appendix E.1 compares CIFAR-10 models trained for 100, 300, and 500 epochs through timestep-wise cosine similarity. Appendix E.4 sets Auto-guidance's weight to w=1 for its new comparison. Existing experimental settings in Appendix B are retained; these additions do not establish rerunning the earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix E.1 substantially expands investigation of the central mechanism: additional one-dimensional trajectories, a direct measurement of alignment between model-gap vectors, and annotated two-dimensional trajectories appear in Figures 18–20. Appendix E.4 adds qualitative examination of Auto-guidance artifacts. Earlier scale-sensitivity, inversion-error, and Re-Sampling analyses remain present.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The new results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–14 retain their numerical results. New Table 15 reports Auto-guidance HPS v2/AES/PickScore of 32.1650/6.1187/22.0177 alongside W2SD's retained 33.5959/6.2252/22.3644. New trajectory and qualitative results supplement these comparisons. Figure 19 shows mostly positive alignment but negative values at late plotted timesteps, despite the accompanying uniformly positive interpretation.

T1.justification: v3 corrects the central mathematical quantities from density gradients to log-density gradients in the definitions of the model gaps, Theorem 1, its Appendix D.1 proof, and the inversion-error equations. This repairs the identification of diffusion scores underlying the main formal result, rather than merely changing notation. The proof strategy and neglected-inversion-error assumption remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The conclusion narrows the first-integration claim to weak-to-strong inference enhancement through a reflection mechanism. The principal claims about broad applicability, cumulative improvements, preference gains, and efficiency remain. Replacing 'approximate' with 'bridge' generally preserves their intended meaning.

C2.justification: Appendix E.4 newly attributes reduced distortion and oversaturation to refinement through the score network rather than direct interpolation, and discusses Auto-guidance's weight sensitivity. Appendix E.1 newly interprets cosine alignment as reliable support for bridging the model gaps, but its assertion of consistently acute angles conflicts with Figure 19's negative late-timestep similarities.

D1.justification: The v3 abstract announces publicly available code and provides a repository address, absent from v1. The new appendix experiments document their epoch budgets and Auto-guidance weight. Existing implementation and hyperparameter descriptions are retained; repository availability is only reported by the PDF.

R1.justification: v3 substantially develops positioning against the closely related Auto-guidance work by Karras et al. (2024), adding discussion in Section 3.1, Appendix A, and new Appendix E.4. It acknowledges the shared high-level concept while emphasizing reflection and broader model pairings. Sadat et al. (2024) and Lou and Ermon (2023) are also newly cited in the artifact discussion.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose remain intact. Local revisions clarify score terminology, adjust novelty wording, and update cross-references. Appendix E gains two subsections, while its existing inversion-error and Re-Sampling discussions are retained under new subsection numbers.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 18–20, the Auto-guidance comparison in Figure 23, and Table 15 within the existing presentation style. Former Figures 18–19 become Figures 21–22, and several retained figures and tables move. Existing benchmark displays are preserved rather than substantially redesigned.

improvement.justification: v3 improves mathematical correctness by repairing the score-gradient definitions and proof, provides a relevant Auto-guidance comparison, and adds code-access information. These gains are tempered by overinterpretation of the new alignment evidence: Figure 19 contradicts the claim of positive alignment throughout, and the Auto-guidance comparison examines only w=1. The net improvement is useful but limited.
